extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary officials, and legal counsel involved in practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order resolving a USPTO disciplinary proceeding against a registered patent attorney, stating stipulated facts, legal conclusions, mitigating factors, imposed sanctions, probation conditions, enforcement procedures, publication and notification obligations. This serves as both a disciplinary decision and a template for procedural enforcement of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional basis for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over the matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the statutory and regulatory authority under which disciplinary actions are brought and resolved by the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner registration and applicability of Disciplinary Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is a registered attorney authorized to practice before the USPTO and is subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.P.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that registered practitioners are governed by the USPTO Code and therefore subject to USPTO discipline for misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal conviction as basis for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent self-reported pleading guilty to a class one misdemeanor (child abuse) and accepted a two-year deferred judgment/sentence with conditions; the criminal conviction was the underlying basis for discipline imposed by the Office of Regulation Counsel in Denver, Colorado.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal convictions, particularly those involving moral turpitude or conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice, can form the factual basis for professional discipline by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific disciplinary rule violations alleged
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledged conduct violated Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility: Rule 1023(b)(5) by engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice; Rule 1023(b)(6) by engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on Respondent's fitness to practice before the Office; and Rules 1023(a) and 1023(b)(5) and (6) via 1023(c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the exact regulatory provisions relied upon to characterize the misconduct; these rule citations form the legal basis for sanctioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors considered
rubrics_metrics.description: The order lists mitigating factors: respondent was in compliance with his criminal sentence; had completed the anger management evaluation; had completed the parenting class; was scheduling community service hours; voluntarily saw his therapist more frequently after the event; expressed remorse throughout the investigation; parenting time with his daughter was not changed; and respondent had no prior disciplinary history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors were weighed in determining the agreed sanction (stayed suspension and probation) and serve as examples of circumstances that may mitigate discipline in similar cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed sanction — stayed suspension with probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practicing before the USPTO for sixty (60) days, with execution of the suspension immediately stayed so long as respondent serves and successfully completes a twenty-four month probationary period commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stayed suspension plus probation is an available sanction where mitigating factors justify deferral of actual suspension contingent on compliance with conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation condition — comply with terms of criminal sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: During the probationary period respondent must comply with the terms of his criminal sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with the criminal sentence is a violation of the probation conditions and may trigger enforcement steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation condition — no further violations of USPTO Code
rubrics_metrics.description: During probation respondent shall not conduct himself in any fashion that would constitute misconduct in violation of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued compliance with professional conduct rules is an express condition of staying the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation condition — complete one-day ethics school
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must attend, pay for, and successfully pass the one-day ethics school offered by the Office of Attorney Regulation Counsel within the time prescribed by the March 31, 2011 order accepting the stipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandated continuing-education (ethics school) can be imposed as part of probation to remediate professional conduct issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation condition — independent mental health examination and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must obtain an independent mental health examination from a provider approved by the OARC within thirty days from date the OARC approves the provider, but no longer than ninety days from the date the stipulation is approved; follow the recommendations of the provider; provide proof of compliance as necessary on a quarterly basis after providing appropriate releases; and timely provide all reports to the Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mental health evaluation and compliance with treatment recommendations can be required and monitored as a condition of professional probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice allowed during probation unless stay lifted
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is permitted to practice patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO during his probationary period unless the stay of the suspension is lifted by order of the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stayed suspension permits continued practice subject to probation terms; lifting the stay imposes immediate restriction of practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement procedure — Order to Show Cause for suspected noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not order that the stay be lifted and respondent be immediately suspended for up to sixty days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the initial procedural step the OED takes to address alleged probation violations and to seek activation of the stayed suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement procedure — service and response period
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order to Show Cause shall be sent to respondent at the last address of record furnished pursuant to 37 C.P.R. § 11.11(a), and respondent shall be granted fifteen (15) days to respond to the Order to Show Cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies notice method and a firm 15-day response window for the practitioner to reply to allegations of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement escalation to USPTO Director
rubrics_metrics.description: After the 15-day response period, if the OED Director continues to believe respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director: (i) the Order to Show Cause, (ii) respondent's response, and (iii) evidence and argument supporting lifting the stay and requesting that the USPTO Director immediately lift the stay of suspension and suspend respondent for up to sixty days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines how OED packages the matter for decision by the USPTO Director and seeks activation of suspension as an enforcement remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if suspension is activated — dissociation of USPTO identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: If respondent is suspended pursuant to the enforcement provisions: (1) the USPTO shall promptly dissociate respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates; (2) respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated; and (3) respondent may not obtain a USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies immediate technical and administrative steps to prevent access to USPTO systems and filings upon suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: No stay of suspension pending review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director lifts the stay of the suspension and respondent seeks review of that decision, any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the immediate suspension of respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that seeking review does not delay the effect of an imposed suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may seek additional discipline under other provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Settlement Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from seeking discipline against respondent in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57 for the misconduct that caused the stay to be lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves the Office's right to pursue separate or additional disciplinary proceedings under the fuller disciplinary provisions of the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the supplied Notice of Stayed Suspension and Probation language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires public disclosure of the disciplinary action via the OED Reading Room and Official Gazette with specified content describing the discipline and underlying misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates out-of-office notification to relevant state enforcement bodies and courts of record of public disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including this Final Order, when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct and/or in any future disciplinary proceeding (a) as an aggravating factor in determining discipline and/or (b) to rebut any statement or representation by or on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the decision and underlying facts can be relied upon in future disciplinary contexts and may aggravate future sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies each party bears its own costs rather than the imposition of costs or fines payable by respondent to the Office in this settlement.
